title: Lesson 29: Testing Integrations: Mocking, Sandbox Test Strategy, and Integration Test Suites
description: How to prove an integration works: mocking callouts and classes to unit test your Apex, choosing the right sandbox for each kind of test, and assembling suites that prove the seams hold.

questions.question: Why must a test that exercises an external callout register a mock rather than reach the live service?
options: Because real callouts are slow to run but still reach the live external service during a test run.
Because no real network calls happen in test context, so a mock supplies the response.
Because the external vendor blocks every request that comes from a test run.
Because callout logic cannot be covered by any automated test.
questions.explanation: The platform refuses the network call while a test runs, so the mock is how the test states what the external system would have returned and pins down how the code should react.

questions.question: Which sandbox type is the one that supports performance and load testing of an integration path?
options: A Developer sandbox, because it refreshes the fastest.
A Developer Pro sandbox, because it raises the data allowance.
A Partial Copy sandbox, because it copies a template-defined subset of records.
A Full sandbox, because it is a complete replica of production.
questions.explanation: Load and performance testing need the whole org, and the full replica is the only sandbox type where that level of testing is supported.

questions.question: What does wrapping the exercised code in the start-test and stop-test calls give a test?
options: A fresh set of governor limits and synchronous execution of queued async work.
A rollback of every DML operation so that the org data is left completely untouched.
A way to run the test without registering a callout mock first.
An automatic retry of any assertion that fails the first time.
questions.explanation: The wrapped section runs under its own limit budget, and queued async work is flushed synchronously at the stop call so the test can assert on the result without waiting.
